selection: The first published river gauges (ADR-136): the four rivers that flow toward Lake Powell named in the recent-conditions plan, directed by Brian Busch on 2026-10-27 as the first set to publish. Each is a Utah gauge from gauge-review.csv with a 1991-2020 record and a traced basin within 25% of its published drainage area. Under the tier ruling recorded as ADR-137, each is shaped: three have a published reservoir inside the basin, and the Dirty Devil's inventoried dams hold at least 10% of a year's flow. Each gauge's daily mean flow is published without a comparison with normal and without a rank. The tier was taken from the worksheet's suggestion at Brian's direction and is pending his formal ruling in the review page; reviewer_ruling in gauge-review.csv is still blank for all four. No gauge here is a reservoir's inflow, and no two are ever added together.

09379500.usgs_name: SAN JUAN RIVER NEAR BLUFF, UT

tier.basis: ADR-137: a published reservoir sits inside the traced basin. Navajo Reservoir is the largest.

evidence.largest_dams: Navajo Dam (1,986,600 AF); Vallecito Dam (136,200 AF); Ridges Basin Dam (135,721 AF)
evidence.trace: traced; NLDI basin 22,667 sq mi against a published 23,000

flows_toward.name: Lake Powell
flows_toward.evidence: The gauge is in subbasin 14080205, inside the Upper Colorado region (HUC 14), which is the Colorado River basin above Lee Ferry. The San Juan River below the gauge ends in Lake Powell's San Juan arm. Lake Powell is a reservoir on the storage map; this gauge is not its inflow.
